lem-qsm-local-hermitian-diagonalization:
## Statement

For every integer $d\ge1$ and Hermitian matrix $A\in M_d(\mathbb C)$, there is
an orthonormal basis of $\mathbb C^d$ consisting of eigenvectors of $A$, and
all eigenvalues are real. If in addition $x^*Ax\ge0$ for every $x\in\mathbb
C^d$, every eigenvalue is nonnegative and the matrix $A^{1/2}$ obtained by
replacing each eigenvalue by its nonnegative square root is well defined.
def-qsm-local-finite-tensor-state:
## Definition

Fix an integer $q\ge1$, let $V=\mathbb C^q$ with its standard ordered
orthonormal basis $(|j\rangle)_{j=1}^q$, and use the inner-product convention
that is linear in the first argument. For each integer $N\ge0$, write
$V_N=V^{\otimes N}$ with the displayed factor order; $V_0=\mathbb C$.
The lexicographically ordered product vectors form the chosen basis of
$V_N$, as in [[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]].

A **finite tensor density** on $V_N$ is a density operator in the exact
root-library sense of [[def-qc-density-operator]]: a nonnegative endomorphism
$\rho$ with $\operatorname{Tr}\rho=1$. In the standard column coordinates
this means $\rho=\rho^*$ and $x^*\rho x\ge0$ for every $x$.

A **bounded observable matrix** on $V_N$ is a Hermitian matrix $A=A^*$,
with operator norm $\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}=\sup_{\|x\|=1}\|Ax\|$. Its
mathematical expectation functional in $\rho$ is
$\omega_\rho(A)=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho A)$. This is a finite matrix trace
pairing; its physical interpretation is supplied separately by a measurement
postulate.

A **finite POVM** with $r\ge1$ outcomes is a family
$M_1,\ldots,M_r$ of nonnegative matrices on $V_N$ with
$\sum_{a=1}^r M_a=I$. Each $M_a$ is an **effect**, meaning $0\le M_a\le I$;
the upper bound follows because $I-M_a=\sum_{b\ne a}M_b\ge0$. The numbers
$\operatorname{Tr}(\rho M_a)$ are its finite trace pairings. They are
nonnegative and normalized when read as outcome probabilities under the
adopted physical Born rule. Here $M\ge0$ means $M=M^*$ and
$x^*Mx\ge0$ for every column vector $x$. This definition alone does not
adopt the physical probability rule.
def-qsm-local-finite-matrix-entropy:
## Definition

For a finite tensor density $\rho$ on $V_N$, list its eigenvalues with
multiplicity as $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_{q^N}$. The finite Hermitian
diagonalization in [[lem-qsm-local-hermitian-diagonalization]] and positivity
of $\rho$ give $\lambda_i\ge0$ and $\sum_i\lambda_i=1$. Define its
**dimensionless spectral entropy**, measured in nats, by
$$s_N(\rho):=-\sum_{i:\lambda_i>0}\lambda_i\log\lambda_i,$$
with $0\log0:=0$. This is independent of the ordering of the eigenvalues,
including when eigenvalues are repeated. It contains no physical entropy
unit; here $\log$ is the natural logarithm of [[def-natural-logarithm]],
and a later physical postulate may assign $S_N=k_Bs_N$.
def-qsm-local-additive-spectral-ensemble:
## Definition

Fix $q\ge1$ and real level parameters $e_1,\ldots,e_q$. Use the real
exponential of [[def-real-exponential-function-and-e]] and natural logarithm
of [[def-natural-logarithm]]. For $N\ge1$, define
the one-site diagonal matrix $h|j\rangle=e_j|j\rangle$ and, for
$a=1,\ldots,N$,
$$h^{(a)}=I^{\otimes(a-1)}\otimes h\otimes I^{\otimes(N-a)},\qquad H_N=\sum_{a=1}^N h^{(a)}.$$
Thus the product basis vector $|j_1,\ldots,j_N\rangle$ has eigenvalue
$E(j_1,\ldots,j_N)=\sum_{a=1}^N e_{j_a}$; repeated level values remain
distinct basis labels and therefore count as degeneracy.

For finite $\beta\in\mathbb R$, put
$$Z_1=\sum_{j=1}^q e^{-\beta e_j},\qquad p_j=\frac{e^{-\beta e_j}}{Z_1},\qquad E=\sum_{j=1}^q p_je_j.$$
All terms in $Z_1$ are positive, so $Z_1>0$. Define the one-site canonical
density $\gamma=\operatorname{diag}(p_1,\ldots,p_q)$. For $N$ sites put
$$Z_N=\sum_{(j_1,\ldots,j_N)\in\{1,\ldots,q\}^N} e^{-\beta\sum_{a=1}^N e_{j_a}},\qquad \gamma_N=\operatorname{diag}\left( \frac{e^{-\beta\sum_{a=1}^N e_{j_a}}}{Z_N}\right)_ {(j_1,\ldots,j_N)\in\{1,\ldots,q\}^N}.$$
The mathematical definition permits $\beta=0$ and negative $\beta$ as well
as positive $\beta$; a physical positive-temperature interpretation is a
separate assumption.

For a width $\delta_N\ge0$, define the spectral band label set and its
projection by
$$\Gamma_N=\left\{(j_1,\ldots,j_N): \left|\sum_{a=1}^N e_{j_a}-NE\right|\le\delta_N\right\},\qquad \Pi_N=\sum_{\mathbf j\in\Gamma_N}|\mathbf j\rangle\langle\mathbf j|.$$
Its rank is $\Omega_N=\operatorname{Tr}\Pi_N=|\Gamma_N|$, which counts
all basis vectors in the band, including degeneracy. When $\Omega_N>0$,
define the normalized band density $\sigma_N=\Pi_N/\Omega_N$. If
$\Omega_N=0$, this normalized density is undefined.
lem-qsm-local-subsystem-trace-tests:
## Statement

Let $V_A,V_B$ be nonzero finite-dimensional tensor registers and let $\rho$
be a finite tensor density on $V_A\otimes V_B$. Then
$$\rho_A:=\operatorname{Tr}_B\rho$$
is a finite tensor density on $V_A$. For every matrix $A$ on $V_A$,
$$\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_AA)=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho(A\otimes I_B)).$$
For a finite POVM $(M_a)_{a=1}^r$ on $V_A$, the trace pairings of its
outcomes in $\rho_A$ equal the trace pairings of the lifted effects
$M_a\otimes I_B$ in $\rho$.
def-qsm-local-matrix-net-completion:
## Definition

Fix $q\ge1$ and the ordered registers $V_N=(\mathbb C^q)^{\otimes N}$,
with $V_0=\mathbb C$. Here $\operatorname{End}(V_N)$ is the space of linear
maps $V_N\to V_N$ as in [[def-linear-map]]. For such a map define its
operator norm by $\|A\|:=\sup_{\|x\|=1}\|Ax\|$, using the ordered tensor
inner product of [[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]], and let $A^*$ be
its adjoint. Embed $\mathcal A_N=\operatorname{End}(V_N)$ into
$\mathcal A_{N+1}$ by
$\iota_N(A)=A\otimes I_q$. Write a vector in $V_N\otimes\mathbb C^q$ as
$x=\sum_{j=1}^q x_j\otimes|j\rangle$. Then
$$\|(A\otimes I_q)x\|^2=\sum_{j=1}^q\|Ax_j\|^2 \le\|A\|^2\sum_{j=1}^q\|x_j\|^2=\|A\|^2\|x\|^2.$$
Testing on unit simple tensors $v\otimes|1\rangle$ and taking the supremum
over unit $v$ gives the reverse norm inequality, hence
$\|A\otimes I_q\|=\|A\|$. The embeddings are isometric unital
*-homomorphisms. For $m\ge N$, define
$\iota_{N,m}(A)=A\otimes I_q^{\otimes(m-N)}$ and identify
$A\in\mathcal A_N$ with its image at every larger register. For a two-step
inclusion the maps fit into this commutative diagram:

```tikzcd
\mathcal A_N \arrow[r,"\iota_N"] \arrow[rr,bend right=16,"\iota_{N,N+2}"'] & \mathcal A_{N+1} \arrow[r,"\iota_{N+1}"] & \mathcal A_{N+2}
```

The curved arrow tensors with two identities, and the upper path tensors with
one identity twice; both send $A$ to $A\otimes I_q\otimes I_q$. Let
$\mathcal A_{\rm loc}=\bigcup_{N\ge0}\mathcal A_N$ with the
induced norm, product and adjoint. Define $\mathcal A=\overline{\mathcal
A_{\rm loc}}$ in this norm. This is the
quasilocal matrix algebra for the one-dimensional ordered register chain; it
is a unital C*-algebra with unit the common image of $1\in\mathcal A_0$.

The sequence $(\mathcal A_N,\iota_N)$ is the specified inductive system.
This definition concerns one fixed local matrix size $q$ and makes no claim
about a physical lattice geometry or dynamics.

post-qsm-local-ensemble-preparations.physical_scope: Adopted preparation assignments for the explicitly finite, noninteracting q-level tensor model: canonical finite-temperature density and, when nonempty, a uniform exact energy-band density. These rules are conditional model inputs; they do not assert dynamical thermalization, experimental frequencies, data, or a continuum or interacting limit.

post-qsm-local-ensemble-preparations:
## Postulate

For the finite $q$-level tensor model of
[[def-qsm-local-additive-spectral-ensembles]], adopt the following
preparation rules in addition to the state and outcome assumptions P1 and P2
of [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] and
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]. The quantities in this
item are model assignments; they are not inferred from the cited texts or
from data.

1. For declared temperature $T>0$ kelvin and Boltzmann constant
   $k_B>0$ joules per kelvin, use $\beta=(k_BT)^{-1}>0$ joules$^{-1}$ and
   assign the canonical finite density $\gamma_N$ of
   [[def-qsm-local-additive-spectral-ensembles]].
2. For declared band width $\delta_N\ge0$ in joules, if its label set
   $\Gamma_N$ is nonempty, the uniform band preparation is the density
   $\sigma_N=\Pi_N/|\Gamma_N|$ from that definition. If the set is empty,
   this normalized preparation is undefined and no band state is assigned.
3. For a stated finite POVM $(M_a)$ on the register, the outcome law is the
   adopted Born law $p_a=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho M_a)$ of P2. A prediction is
   the resulting model probability, not a reported detector frequency.

The positive-temperature interpretation uses SI units as fixed in
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. No preparation mechanism,
thermalization process, sampling law, apparatus error, or observed data is
asserted. A statement that a physical preparation realizes one of these
densities requires a separate empirical identification and uncertainty
analysis.
lem-qsm-local-tensor-gibbs-factorization:
## Statement

Use the finite additive spectral data of
[[def-qsm-local-additive-spectral-ensembles]]. For every $N\ge1$,
$Z_N=Z_1^N$ and $\gamma_N=\gamma^{\otimes N}$. Its first $k$-site reduced
density is $\gamma^{\otimes k}$ for $1\le k\le N$, and its expected additive
energy is $NE$.
thm-qsm-local-classical-diagonal-embeddi:
## Statement

Let $q\ge1$ and let $\mu_N$ be probability laws on
$\{1,\ldots,q\}^N$ for $N\ge1$, consistent under deleting the last
coordinate. On a local matrix $A\in\mathcal A_N$, define
$$\omega_N(A)=\sum_{x\in\{1,\ldots,q\}^N}\mu_N(x)A_{xx}.$$
In particular, for a diagonal $D_f$ this is
$\omega_N(D_f)=\sum_x\mu_N(x)f(x)$. On the algebra $\mathcal A$ of
[[def-qsm-local-matrix-net-completion]],
Then this rule extends uniquely to a state on $\mathcal A$. The theorem
constructs a classical diagonal state; it does not say that every state on
$\mathcal A$ is diagonal or classical.
thm-qsm-local-independent-shell-equivale:
## Statement

Fix $q\ge1$, real one-site levels $e_j$, finite $\beta\in\mathbb R$, and
the ensembles of [[def-qsm-local-additive-spectral-ensembles]]. Suppose for
every $N$ the band width obeys
$$\delta_N\ge q\sum_{j=1}^q|e_j|,\qquad \delta_N/N\longrightarrow0.$$
Then every band is nonempty. For each fixed $k\ge1$ and $N\ge k$, let
$\sigma_{N,k}=\operatorname{Tr}_{k+1,\ldots,N}\sigma_N$ and
$\gamma_k=\gamma^{\otimes k}$. Then
$$\|\sigma_{N,k}-\gamma_k\|_1\to0,\qquad \frac1N s_N(\sigma_N)\to -\sum_{j=1}^q p_j\log p_j.$$
Here $\|D\|_1$ for a Hermitian finite matrix is the sum of absolute values
of its eigenvalues, and $s_N$ is dimensionless spectral entropy. This is an
independent finite-alphabet result; it asserts neither global trace-norm
convergence nor an interacting or continuous-model equivalence.

def-qsm-local-coercive-regulated-model.physical_scope: A fixed finite-mode coercive real polynomial form Hamiltonian, its selected self-adjoint form realization and trace-class Gibbs operator, with normal-state Born interpretation conditional on the current batch-36 QSM postulate, whose readiness is unresolved. There is no regulator removal, continuum interacting QFT, or empirical realization claim.

def-qsm-local-coercive-regulated-model:
## Definition

Fix a finite integer $r\ge1$, positive coefficients $a_j$, a real polynomial
$V$ on $\mathbb R^r$, and constants $c>0,C_0\ge0$ such that
$V(q)\ge c|q|^2-C_0$. Use the QFT supplier's form realization of
[[def-qft-regulated-polynomial-hamiltonian]] and
[[thm-qft-self-adjoint-regulated-interaction]] on
$L^2(\mathbb R^r,dq)$, and denote its self-adjoint operator by $h$. This
item's **regulated interacting model** is the tuple of these finite data,
the selected form realization, and an energy scale $E_*>0$ joules, with
$H=E_*h$. The coordinate $q$ and coefficients are dimensionless rescaled
model parameters unless another dimensional map is explicitly supplied.
The finite polynomial may couple coordinates; no limit in $r$ is included.

For each $b>0$, [[thm-qft-regulated-gibbs-trace]] proves
$\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-b h})<\infty$ and positivity. Thus for physical
$\beta>0$ in joules$^{-1}$, $b=\beta E_*>0$ and
$$\rho_\beta=\frac{e^{-\beta H}}{Z_\beta},\qquad Z_\beta=\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\beta H})\in(0,\infty)$$
is a trace-one positive trace-class density. Its interpretation as a normal
quantum measurement state uses the current batch-36 draft carrier
[[post-qsm-normal-measurement-state]], which adopts a trace-class density on a
specified separable Hilbert space and the PVM Born law
$\mathbb P_\rho\{A\in C\}=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho E_A(C))$. This interface
matches the mathematical state constructed here. The mathematical probability and bounded trace-pairing inputs now have exact canonical suppliers through the trace-state calculus. The normal-state interpretation remains an adopted physical premise; source adoption is separate from native readiness and empirical validation. The QFT mathematical trace theorem remains the mathematical supplier.

This selected finite-regulator realization does not assert essential
self-adjointness of the bare compact-support differential expression, a
unique realization among all self-adjoint extensions, regulator removal, or
an interacting continuum theory.

pthm-qsm-local-qualified-shell-measureme.physical_scope: Conditional predictions for a specified finite q-level noninteracting tensor model, adopted canonical and uniform-band preparations, a fixed finite subsystem and a declared finite POVM. No detector frequencies, thermalization, interacting or growing-block conclusion is asserted.

pthm-qsm-local-qualified-shell-measureme:
## Statement

Assume the physical preparation postulate
[[post-qsm-local-ensemble-preparations]], and the exact independent-shell
hypotheses and notation of [[thm-qsm-local-independent-shell-equivalence]].
For each fixed $k$ and each fixed $r$-outcome POVM $(M_a)_{a=1}^r$ on the
$k$-site register, the shell and canonical model outcome probabilities
$p^{\rm sh}_{N,a}$ and $p^{\rm can}_{N,a}$ satisfy
$$\sum_{a=1}^r|p^{\rm sh}_{N,a}-p^{\rm can}_{N,a}|\longrightarrow0.$$
This is a conditional prediction for the adopted states and specified
measurement; it supplies no empirical frequencies or sampling inference.

pthm-qsm-local-regulated-interacting-gib.physical_scope: Conditional finite-mode, coercive polynomial trace-Gibbs model at positive temperature and finite-form-energy normal competitors. The three QSM batch-36 carriers remain drafts; their repaired mathematical inputs now have exact canonical carriers, with native readiness separate. No data, thermalization, regulator removal, or continuum interacting QFT claim is made.

pthm-qsm-local-regulated-interacting-gib:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the finite regulated model of
[[def-qsm-local-coercive-regulated-model]], the current draft thermal
preparation interface [[post-qsm-thermal-gibbs-preparation]], the current
draft normal-state interface [[post-qsm-normal-measurement-state]], and the
current draft mathematical theorem
[[thm-qsm-trace-gibbs-variational]]. Its inspected exact interface is: for a
nonzero separable complex Hilbert space and a densely defined self-adjoint
$A$ bounded below, if $e^{-\beta A}$ is trace class for every $\beta$ in an
open interval $I\subset(0,\infty)$, then $Z_\beta\in(0,\infty)$ and
$\rho_\beta=e^{-\beta A}/Z_\beta$ is a faithful normal density; every normal
density of finite absolute spectral form energy satisfies
$\mathcal E_A(\rho)-TS(\rho)\ge F_\beta$, with equality exactly at
$\rho=\rho_\beta$. The theorem assumes AC. Under these conditions, for each
$\beta>0$ J$^{-1}$ the model state is
$\rho_\beta=e^{-\beta E_*h}/Z_\beta$, with $0<Z_\beta<\infty$, and the
stated free-energy inequality holds for every normal density $\rho$ whose
spectral law $\mu_\rho(C)=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho E_H(C))$ has finite first
absolute moment $\int|\lambda|\,d\mu_\rho(\lambda)<\infty$. The energy
$\mathcal E_H(\rho)=\int\lambda\,d\mu_\rho(\lambda)$ and free energy are in
joules, entropy $S(\rho)$ is in joules per kelvin, and $T>0$ is in kelvin.
The conditional result is for the selected fixed finite-mode form
realization. It asserts no cutoff removal or empirical realization.
cex-qsm-local-empty-exact-band:
## Statement

There are two-level additive data and a canonical mean for which every
zero-width band centered at that mean is empty. Consequently a normalized
uniform band density is not defined for that choice.
cex-qsm-local-entropy-density-insufficie:
## Statement

There are finite density sequences whose dimensionless entropy per site has
the same limit as a canonical product density while their one-site reduced
states remain separated by a fixed trace norm.
cex-qsm-local-local-global-distinction:
## Statement

For every $N\ge2$ there are diagonal densities on $N$ binary registers whose
every proper fixed-size marginal equals the corresponding maximally mixed
marginal, while their global trace-norm distance remains one. A global
two-outcome POVM distinguishes the states with probability gap $1/2$.
